newsitem.title: NEPAL: Two killed in Nepal local polls violence.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in Nepal local polls violence.

text.p: Two men were killed in clashes between rival political groups during the final phase of Nepal's local elections, police said on Monday.
One was shot dead on Monday in Dhanusa district. The other was killed late on Sunday in neighbouring Rautahat district in central Nepal.
Voters in 35 districts are choosing new village development committees and municipal authorities, which are the Himalayan kingdom's equivalent of local councils.
Police fired in the air and lobbed teargas shells to separate rival political groups in other parts of the country, officials said.
About 10 people have been killed during a month of election-related violence. Monday was the second and final phase of polling.
Results from last week's polling put the communists, who are part of the ruling coalition, strongly ahead of the centrist opposition in most local bodies.
About 190,000 representatives will be elected in 4,000 village committees and 58 municipalities for a five-year term.
